You can try to build SparkR from source on Windows using the instructions at https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/blob/master/BUILDING.md with the Hadoop version set to 2.4.1. Longer term we could have binary versions for commonly used Hadoop versions.

Re: Connect a Windows client to Spark cluster

From the error message it looks like the Spark client was not able to connect to the Spark cluster. This could happen due to a few reasons

1. The Spark versions running on the SparkR driver and cluster are different. You can check this by verifying the Spark version being included in the maven build.

2. There are some ports which the SparkR driver (actually the Spark context) is trying to use and is unable to do so. AFAIK Spark requires that the driver have a externally visible IP address and the ability to talk over randomly assigned ports between the cluster and the driver. I think there are configuration options that allow one to control what the driver hostname and ports to use should be (See the networking section in http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html) but I haven't tried it out before.

Re: Connect a Windows client to Spark cluster

Nilesh Patil Thanks a lot for sending the stack trace. There is an assumption in SparkR that the library is installed in the same location in the driver and in the cluster. Obviously this will not be true for driver program on windows connecting to a Linux cluster.

I've created a PR (https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/103) that will allow you to pass in sparkRLibDir while calling sparkR.init. You can pass the directory SparkR is installed in the cluster using this. For example on my Macbook, SparkR is installed at /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library/SparkR. So I'll need to pass /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library as sparkRLibDir.

Let me know if this helps.
